Changes are coming to Kitco Pool - Metal Accounts on January 1, 2027

Effective January 1, 2027

What’s changing

Two important changes are coming to Kitco Pool.

A new annual storage fee

We’re introducing an annual storage fee based on the value of the metals you hold in Pool.

There's a $15 annual minimum, and it counts toward your fee for the year. It's not an extra charge.

We’re saying goodbye to transaction fees

You’ll no longer pay transaction fees when you buy or sell metals in Pool.

So you can trade more often without paying transaction fees each time.

Why we’re making this change

For many years, Kitco has covered the cost of storing metals held in Pool without charging a separate storage fee. As those costs have increased, we’re introducing a storage fee to help offset them, based on the metals you hold and their value.

What stays the same

  • The Pool experience stays the same
    You can continue to buy, sell and hold metals in Pool just as you do today.
  • 24/7 online trading
    Buy and sell metals in Pool online whenever it works for you.
  • Low spreads
    Continue to benefit from competitive Pool buy and sell pricing.
  • Fully insured holdings
    The metals supporting your Pool Metal Account remain fully insured by Kitco.

Annual storage rates

The following annual storage rates will apply to the metals you hold in Pool:

iYour storage fee is calculated daily, based on the metals you hold and their value that day.
$15 annual minimum applies per Pool Metal Account and counts toward your storage fees for the year. It isn’t added on top.
MetalAnnual rate
Gold0.12%
Silver0.30%
Platinum0.12%
Palladium0.12%
Rhodium0.40%

How your storage fee works

1

Your daily holdings

We look at the type and amount of metals you hold in Pool each day.

2

Their daily value

We use the daily market price to determine the value of your metals.

3

Your storage rate

We apply that day’s portion of the applicable annual storage rate.

4

Your storage fee accumulates

Those daily amounts add up throughout the year.

Your storage fee reflects what you actually hold. Changes in metal prices, as well as any metals you buy or sell in Pool, are reflected in the daily calculation.

Key dates

When you’ll be billed and updated

1

January 1, 2027

You’ll receive an invoice for the $15 annual minimum.

The $15 counts toward your storage fees for 2027.

2

Throughout 2027

Your storage fee accumulates daily.

We’ll provide quarterly updates so you can see how your storage fees are tracking. We’ll email you when each update is available in your account.

3

January 2028

Your 2027 storage fee is finalized.

If your total storage fee for 2027 is more than the $15 minimum, you’ll receive an invoice for the remaining balance. If it’s $15 or less, there’s nothing more to pay for 2027.

How you’ll be able to pay

You’ll be able to pay your storage fees using Pool holdings, funds on your account or a credit card.

  • Your Pool holdings
  • Funds on your account
  • Credit card
We’ll keep you posted

We’ll reach out by email when the option to choose your preferred payment method is available in your online account.

If you’re considering your options

You can keep your metals in Pool, sell your Pool holdings, exchange them for physical metals, or explore other Kitco storage options, including VaultChain™ and Kitco Allocated Storage. If you’d like to talk through your options, our Customer Experience team is happy to help.

  • Keep your metals in Pool
  • Sell your Pool holdings
  • Exchange for physical metals
  • Explore other Kitco storage options

Frequently asked questions

Select a question to see the answer.

About the changes
For many years, Kitco has covered the cost of storing metals held in Pool without charging a separate storage fee. As those costs have increased, we’re introducing a storage fee to help offset them. The fee is based on the metals you hold and their value.
The new storage fees take effect January 1, 2027.
Yes. You’ll no longer pay the $14.99 online or $19.99 phone transaction fee when you buy or sell metals in Pool.
The metals you hold in Pool will continue to be stored in secure depositories and will be fully insured by Kitco.
We’ll keep you updated by email before the changes take effect, including when you can choose your preferred payment method in your online account.
Understanding your storage fee
Your storage fee is calculated daily based on the type and amount of metals you hold, their daily market value and the applicable annual storage rate. Those daily amounts are added together throughout the year.
For gold, silver, platinum and palladium, we use the daily Kitco fix to determine the value of your holdings. Rhodium is valued using its daily market price. Learn more about the Kitco fix.
Yes. Because your storage fee is based on the daily value of your holdings, changes in metal prices will affect the amount that accumulates each day.
Your storage fee adjusts automatically based on what you actually hold each day. If you buy more, those holdings are included from that point forward. If you sell, you stop accumulating storage fees on the metals you no longer hold.
Each metal is calculated using its applicable storage rate. The daily amounts are then combined as part of your total storage fee.
Understanding the $15 annual minimum
No. The $15 minimum counts toward your storage fees for the year. It isn’t an additional fee on top.
No. It’s one $15 annual minimum per Pool Metal Account, even if you hold more than one metal.
The $15 annual minimum still applies, but you won’t owe anything more for that year.
The $15 you’ve already paid is applied toward your total storage fees. You’ll only be invoiced for the remaining balance.
Your storage fees stop accumulating once you no longer hold metals in Pool. The $15 annual minimum you paid for the year is not prorated or refunded.
If you don’t hold any metals in Pool, the $15 annual minimum does not apply.
Billing and payment
You’ll receive an invoice for the $15 annual minimum on January 1, 2027. That amount counts toward your storage fees for 2027.
We’ll provide quarterly updates throughout 2027 showing how your storage fees are accumulating. We’ll email you when each update is available in your account.
No. The quarterly updates are for information only. There’s nothing to pay at that time.
After the end of 2027, we’ll finalize your storage fee for the year. If it’s more than the $15 minimum you already paid, you’ll receive an invoice in January 2028 for the remaining balance.
You’ll be able to pay using Pool holdings, funds on your account or a credit card. We’ll let you know when the option to choose your preferred payment method is available.
